name: realistic-failure-loss

finding.title: `Replace` deletes the stored file before the upload, so an upload that breaks off loses the user's file
finding.description: `Replace` deletes the old object first and then streams `body` into `Upload`. When the upload fails, such as when the client's connection drops while it streams the request body or the bucket returns an error, `Replace` returns the error with the old file already gone and no new one stored. The user's file is lost.

checks: files/store.go:14 streams the request body as the client sends it
files/store.go:17 deletes the old object first

finding.suggestedFix: Upload to a temporary key first, and replace the old object only once the upload succeeded.

+package files
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"io"
+)
+
+// Store keeps each user's files in an object storage bucket.
+type Store struct {
+	bucket Bucket
+}
+
+// Replace stores a new version of a user's file in place of the old one. The
+// upload handler calls it with the request body as the client streams it.
+func (s *Store) Replace(ctx context.Context, userID, name string, body io.Reader) error {
+	key := userID + "/" + name
+	if err := s.bucket.Delete(ctx, key); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	return s.bucket.Upload(ctx, key, body)
+}
